title: We built a remote MCP that lets AI assistants operate the full social management loop
snippet:
We just released a remote MCP that gives Claude, ChatGPT, and other compatible AI clients 23 tools for social and community management.
For anyone using MCPs to either build your own apps or automate workflows, I'd love to get any feedback on additional tools we could add to the MCP!
The MCP connects the assistant to the actual accounts, community activity, analytics, brand voice, and approval queue of a brand.
It can:
• inspect connected accounts and recent activity
• analyse analytics and sentiment across platforms
• identify comments, mentions, and replies worth answering
• understand the existing brand voice
• draft posts, polls, and replies from real audience signals
• schedule or publish approved content
• compare the results with what happened afterward
The most important design decision was separating access from autonomy.
Reading account data works immediately. Anything that can publish requires an additional permission. Generated content first lands in a review queue, and nothing is sent without explicit approval.
We also had to distinguish live social data from stored historical activity, return partial results when one platform fails, and prevent the assistant from treating missing analytics as zero.
The MCP is fully launched and free to try.
Website: [https://fanbase.gg/features/mcp](https://fanbase.gg/features/mcp)
Setup: [https://fanbase.gg/blog/fanbase-mcp](https://fanbase.gg/blog/fanbase-mcp)

title: commas-cli
snippet:
# Commas CLI
Run your [Commas](https://commas.com) (formerly FanBasis) business from the terminal. The CLI is a thin client for the Commas MCP server — every command maps to an MCP tool, so the CLI automatically stays in sync with the server's capabilities.

```
commas login                 # prompts for your API key (stored in ~/.commas/config.json, mode 0600)
commas status                # server health + current config
commas tools                 # list every tool the server exposes
```

Commands run against **production** (`https://www.fanbasis.com`) by default. The sandbox is `https://api-sandbox.commas.net` and needs its own API key, created in the sandbox dashboard at [https://sandbox.commas.net](https://sandbox.commas.net) (Account → API Keys). Keys from the old QA dashboard (qa.dev-fan-basis.com) do not work there. Check and add one with:
```
commas keys list                  # which environments have a key
commas keys add sandbox           # prompts for the key, no echo
```
If you ask for sandbox without one, the command stops and tells you — it will never quietly fall back to production.
The server tracks production vs sandbox per MCP session, so the CLI persists your choice locally and re-applies it on every run:
```
commas env               # show current default
commas env sandbox       # all future commands run against the sandbox
commas env production
commas tx list --env sandbox   # one-off override
```
If the sandbox switch fails, the command aborts rather than silently running against production.

## Configuration
Resolution order: command flags → environment variables → `~/.commas/config.json` → defaults.
| Setting | Flag | Env var | Config key |
|---|---|---|---|
| API key | `--api-key` | `COMMAS_API_KEY` | `apiKey` |
| Server URL | `--server` | `COMMAS_MCP_URL` | `serverUrl` |
| Environment | `--env` | `COMMAS_ENV` | `environment` |
Default server: `https://hearty-flow-production.up.railway.app/mcp`

title: Fanvue API Documentation
snippet:
The Fanvue MCP server exposes the Fanvue API over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), as tools a client calls against the account you sign in with. Once it’s connected, the client can read and answer chats, publish posts, manage the vault and read earnings for your account, or for every creator you manage as an agency. You need a Fanvue creator or agency account and a client that supports MCP. There’s nothing to build and no code to write: connecting is a settings change in the client, and you authorise it through Fanvue OAuth in your browser.
## Quick connect
The server URL is the same for every client:
```
https://mcp.fanvue.com/mcp
```
Add the URL as a remote server in your client, then sign in with Fanvue when the client asks. Two clients offer a one-click install in Detailed setup. Once you’re connected, try the [example requests](/docs/mcp-server/examples). To run the server yourself instead, use the open-source [fanvue-api-mcp](https://github.com/fanvue/fanvue-api-mcp) server.
## Detailed setup
Any client that implements MCP over a remote HTTP connection can connect directly, and any other client can connect through `mcp-remote`. Each client has its own page with the setup steps, requests to try and how to disconnect.

For any other client, use the URL directly if the client supports remote (HTTP) servers, or bridge it with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote):
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"fanvue": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.fanvue.com/mcp"]
}
}
}
```
## What the server can do
The server exposes the previous-version (unversioned) Fanvue API catalogue as tools. Each tool maps to one API operation, and the client picks the tools for each request.
## Read and send messages
Read unread chats and message history, then send replies.
## Read account data
Read your profile, followers, subscribers and notifications.
## Manage posts
Create, edit, pin, repost and schedule posts. Publish an image post from a file.
## Read insights
Read earnings, top spenders and subscriber trends.
## Manage media and the vault
List the vault, organise folders, upload media and grant access.
## Message lists
Read smart lists, create and edit custom lists, then send a mass message to a list.
## Agencies: every managed creator from one connection
With agency scopes, the same connection works against the creator-scoped endpoints for every creator you manage: chats, the chatter leaderboard, per-creator earnings and insights, posts, medi
